# Terms and Conditions

By registering for and participating in the Mixed Signals: V2X Collaborative 3D
Object Detection Challenge (the "Competition"), you agree to the following terms.

## 1. Dataset license and use

A. The Competition uses the Mixed Signals dataset, released under
   [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/). The
   dataset is not redistributed through this platform. You must obtain it from
   the official source (<https://huggingface.co/datasets/sberrio/Mixed-Signals-V2X>)
   and comply with that license.

B. The license permits non-commercial research use with attribution, and
   requires that any redistributed derivatives carry the same license
   (share-alike). Do not use the data commercially or in violation of the license.

C. You must cite the Mixed Signals paper (see the Overview tab) in any
   publication or report that uses the dataset or your Competition results.

## 2. Submissions

A. Submissions consist of prediction files only. Do not attempt to upload or
   execute code that probes, reverse-engineers, or exfiltrates the hidden test
   ground truth.

B. You may not attempt to identify, scrape, or reconstruct the held-out test
   labels by any means other than honest model inference.

C. Each participant or team must use a single account. Creating multiple
   accounts to gain extra submissions or to probe the leaderboard is prohibited
   and will result in disqualification.

D. Per-phase submission limits are enforced by the platform and may be adjusted
   by the organizers if abuse is detected.

## 3. Eligibility, teams and fair play

A. Teams may have one or more members. All members must be registered and a
   member may belong to only one team.

B. Organizers and individuals with access to the hidden test annotations are not
   eligible for prizes.

C. The use of any data, pretrained models, or external resources must comply
   with their respective licenses. If external data or pretrained weights are
   used, organizers may require disclosure for verification.

## 4. Prizes

A. Cash prizes are awarded to the top three entries on the Final (test)
   leaderboard: 1st = 500 USD, 2nd = 300 USD, 3rd = 200 USD. The organizers
   reserve the right to add, modify, withhold, or cancel prizes at their
   discretion.

B. Prize winners will be contacted by the organizers shortly after the
   competition ends, using the contact details associated with their Codabench
   account, to arrange prize delivery. No fixed notification date is guaranteed.

C. Prizes may be subject to applicable laws, taxes, and export restrictions.

## 5. Leaderboard, results and publicity

A. The Development leaderboard is for feedback only and does not determine
   final standings. The Final leaderboard determines official rankings.

B. The organizers may publish participant usernames/team names, scores, and
   aggregate statistics.

C. The organizers' decisions on scoring, ranking, eligibility, and rule
   interpretation are final.

## 6. Disclaimer

The Competition, dataset, and scoring software are provided "as is" without
warranty of any kind. The organizers are not liable for any damages arising from
participation. The organizers reserve the right to modify these terms, the
schedule, or the evaluation at any time, with reasonable notice to participants
via the competition pages.

## 7. Contact

For questions, contact the organizers at the email listed on the competition
homepage.

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# Mixed Signals: V2X Collaborative 3D Object Detection Challenge Welcome! This competition runs on the [Mixed Signals](https://mixedsignalsdataset.cs.cornell.edu/) dataset (ICCV 2025). The task is collaborative 3D object detection: given the LiDAR point clouds for a frame from up to four agents (five LiDAR streams), predict 3D bounding boxes for three meta-classes.
Class idClassGrouped from (10 fine-grained classes)
1Vehiclecar, truck, emergency vehicle, bus, electric vehicle, trailer
2Bikemotorbike, bicycle, portable personal mobility
3Pedestrianpedestrian
The sensors see the scene from different positions, so you can choose to fuse their point clouds to fill occlusions and extend the range of detection beyond a single viewpoint. You may use any subset of the agents and any fusion strategy (early, intermediate, or late fusion, or a single-agent baseline). The only requirement is that predictions are expressed in the "top" ego frame and follow the submission format. See the Evaluation & Submission tab for the format and how entries are scored. ## Getting started 1. Download the data. The point clouds, odometry and training labels are on HuggingFace; download what you need and extract it in place: 2. Train a detector. Clone the dev-kit for the PointPillar baselines (no, early, intermediate and late fusion) to build on: . Any approach is allowed, single-agent or fused across the five LiDARs. 3. Build and check a submission. The starting kit has the frame lists, a dataloader, the format spec and a submission checker. Use them to produce one prediction file per frame and validate it before uploading. See the Evaluation & Submission tab. The dataset page and starting kit have the exact commands and file layout. By participating you agree to the dataset's license and terms (see the Terms tab). ## Splits
SplitScenesUsed forGround truth
Train29 scenes (the 33 official train scenes minus the 4 validation)training your modelpublic
Validation4 scenes carved from the training set (mini_9/18/27/36)Development-phase leaderboardnot released
Test4 held-out scenesFinal-phase leaderboardnot released
## Timeline
PhaseDatesScored on
DevelopmentAug 1 to 28, 2026Public validation split, for leaderboard feedback.
FinalAug 29 to Sep 4, 2026Held-out test set of 4 scenes.
Submissions do not carry over between phases. To be ranked in the Final, submit your predictions on the test set yourself before the phase closes. ## Prizes
PlacePrize
🥇 1st500 USD
🥈 2nd300 USD
🥉 3rd200 USD
Rankings are by mAP on the held-out test set. Winners will be contacted by the organizers shortly after the competition ends to arrange their prize. See the Terms tab for eligibility. ## Citation If you use the dataset, please cite: ```bibtex @inproceedings{luo2025mixedsignals, title = {Mixed Signals: A Diverse Point Cloud Dataset for Heterogeneous LiDAR V2X Collaboration}, author = {Luo, Katie Z. and Dao, Minh-Quan and Liu, Zhenzhen and Campbell, Mark and Chao, Wei-Lun and Weinberger, Kilian Q. and Malis, Ezio and Fr\'emont, Vincent and Hariharan, Bharath and Shan, Mao and Worrall, Stewart and Berrio Perez, Julie Stephany}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)}, year = {2025} } ```

pages.title: Evaluation & Submission
pages.content:
# Evaluation & Submission

This page covers how to format a submission and how entries are scored. For the
task, dataset and timeline, see the Overview tab.

## Building predictions

Produce one detection file per evaluation frame, named after that frame's id.
The frame ids you must predict are listed in the starting kit
(`validation_frames.txt` for Development, `test_frames.txt` for Final). Each
line is one detection with nine fields:

```
# cls cx cy cz dx dy dz yaw score
1 12.34 -3.21 0.05 4.10 1.92 1.55 1.5708 0.97
```

* `cls` ∈ {1=Vehicle, 2=Bike, 3=Pedestrian}
* `cx cy cz`: box centre in metres, "top" ego frame
* `dx dy dz`: length, width, height in metres
* `yaw`: heading (rotation about +z) in radians
* `score`: confidence in [0, 1] (used for ranking detections)

Zip the per-frame files at the root of the archive and upload on the Submit tab.
The starting kit's `SUBMISSION_FORMAT.md` is the authoritative spec, with a
sample submission and a format-checker. Run the checker before you upload.

## Evaluation

We follow the official Mixed Signals / OpenCOOD evaluation protocol exactly,
so leaderboard numbers are directly comparable to the dataset paper.

### Metric

* Matching: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) rotated-box IoU between predicted and
  ground-truth boxes (the z/height dimension is not used for matching, in line
  with the dataset benchmark).
* Average Precision (AP): VOC-2010 "all-points" interpolation, the area
  under the precision-recall curve (not the 11-point variant).
* Per class: AP is computed independently for vehicle, bike and
  pedestrian at IoU thresholds 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7.
* Matching rule: within each frame, detections are ranked by descending
  confidence and greedily matched to ground-truth boxes. Each ground-truth box
  can be matched at most once. Unmatched detections (or matches below the IoU
  threshold) are false positives.
* Evaluation range: boxes whose centre falls outside `x, y ∈ [-51.2, 51.2] m`
  are excluded from both predictions and ground truth before scoring.

### Ranking by mAP

The leaderboard is ranked by the headline mAP, the mean of the three per-class
operating points reported in the paper:

```
mAP = mean( Vehicle AP@0.5 , Bike AP@0.5 , Pedestrian AP@0.3 )
```

(Pedestrians are scored at the looser 0.3 IoU because the boxes are small.) The
leaderboard also reports Vehicle and Bike AP at IoU 0.5/0.7 and Pedestrian AP at
IoU 0.3/0.5, matching the published tables, but only mAP decides the ranking.
Ties on mAP are broken by the leaderboard columns left to right (starting with
Vehicle AP@0.5), then by submission time, so earlier submissions rank higher.

### Scoring program

The scoring program is open and downloadable from the Submit / Files
area. It depends only on `numpy` and implements the BEV IoU and VOC AP from
scratch, so you can run it locally against your own validation labels to
reproduce leaderboard scores exactly.

description: A collaborative 3D object detection challenge on the Mixed Signals dataset, a diverse, real-world point cloud dataset for heterogeneous LiDAR V2X collaboration (3 connected vehicles + a roadside unit with dual LiDAR). Fuse the agents' point clouds to detect vehicles, bikes and pedestrians in the bird's-eye-view plane and climb the leaderboard.
